analysis.title: The Memory Meltdown Is Spreading... And Nasdaq Could Be Next
key_insights: Memory stocks are selling off hard. DRAM (the ETF) broke its short-term trend line and its 50-day moving average, and was down another 5% premarket to 51.8.
DRAM is set to register its most oversold reading since the ETF's inception at the open.

MU broke below $1,000 and, in premarket, below both its 100-day moving average and its rising trend line. RSI is set to reach extremely oversold levels. The 200-day moving average remains considerably lower.
South Korea (KOSPI) is described as the epicenter of the weakness in this part of the AI trade.
Goldman's Memory basket fell 9.3% between October 5 and 12 and its AI Semiconductors basket fell 6.7%. Nasdaq underperformed the S&P 500 by 1.7 percentage points over the same period.
Nasdaq futures funding initially looked resilient, but its premium versus S&P futures has started reversing.
CFTC data showed gross Nasdaq futures longs in the Other trader category at one-year highs as of October 6, a potentially vulnerable pocket of positioning.
Goldman sees signs consistent with some recently established length being reduced, but the available data do not confirm the size of any unwind.
The divergence between memory stocks and the broader Nasdaq is extreme. Either memory is overshooting to the downside or the broader tech trade has not yet priced in the weakness.
BofA's FMS shows investors are the most overweight technology since August 2020.
NDX implied volatility remains relatively subdued, so Nasdaq downside hedges still look relatively attractive.
